newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian Solvay proposes 10-for-one stock split.
newsitem.headline: Belgian Solvay proposes 10-for-one stock split.

text.p: Belgian chemicals group Solvay said on Thursday 1996's net dividend would be left unchanged following a fall in underlying earnings but proposed a stock split to make its shares more attractive to investors.

In a final statement on 1996 profit, Solvay said a 2.1 billion Belgian franc gain, mainly on the September sale of its animal health activities to American Home Products Corp , lifted consolidated net earnings nine percent to 13.6 billion francs. But net underlying profit fell eight percent to 11.54 billion francs "because of a drop in plastics margins."

Solvay said the contribution of its plastics division, its second most important in 1995, to EBIT (earnings before debt charges, taxes and other items) fell 60 percent to 3.5 billion francs. Group EBIT fell 12 percent to 21.3 billion francs.

"The board of directors will propose...the payment of a net dividend of 550 francs a share, which is the same level as in 1995," Solvay said. An extraordinary general meeting of shareholders would also be asked to vote on a 10-for-one stock split.
"This stock split is intended to facilitate access to Solvay stock and to bring its value in line with typical U.S. and U.K. share values," Solvay said.

Spokeswoman Dominique Clerbois said the move would not affect Solvay's American Depositary Receipts (ADRs). "At the moment 10 ADRs are equivalent to one Solvay share...afterwards we hope one ADR will be worth the same as one share," she said.
Clerbois noted the United States was Solvay's most important market in terms of sales and was where the company's growth was strongest.
Solvay's shares closed down 25 francs at 20,800 francs ($600) ahead of the news.

In an investor note, Belgian Generale Bank said the dividend news was disappointing. "As Solvay always tries to increase its dividend whenever possible this decision does not look very promising for 1997 expected earnings growth," the bank said.
